The ATO says \"Our systems automatically treat some amounts you earn as employment income or business income. If these amounts aren't the same as your actual employment or business income, you need to make an adjustment at label G.\" It exists because the co-contribution and the low income super tax offset both require at least 10% of total income to come from employment or business.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions, label G","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/adjustment-questions-a1-a4-individual-tax-return-2025/a3-government-super-contributions-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Government super contributions income from employment and business","k":"Dollar adjustment reported at question A3 label G of the individual tax return","def":"Whole dollars at question A3 label G, and it can be negative, in which case an L is printed in the code box beside it. The ATO calls it a proxy, not a fund return: \"Associated earnings are an approximate amount earned from excess contributions while they were in your super fund\", worked out at an average of the quarterly general interest charge rates, compounding daily from 1 July of the year of the breach to the date of the original determination letter. Where it is assessed the taxpayer also gets a non-refundable 15% offset against it, and the excess contributions themselves are released rather than taxed at 47%.","dsrc":"ATO, Non-concessional contributions cap","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/growing-and-keeping-track-of-your-super/caps-limits-and-tax-on-super-contributions/non-concessional-contributions-cap","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Excess non-concessional contributions associated earnings amount","k":"Dollar amount of associated earnings on excess non-concessional super contributions","def":"Whole dollars determined by the ATO, not written by the taxpayer, and inserted into the assessment for the financial year in which the excess contributions were made. The ATO says \"Your level of rebate is calculated on the age of the oldest person covered by the policy. We use the benefit code to apply the right level of rebate\", and that \"The valid benefit codes are 30, 31, 35, 36, 40 and 41.\" Codes 30 and 31 are under 65, 35 and 36 are 65 to 69, and 40 and 41 are 70 or over, with the second of each pair covering 1 April to 30 June.","dsrc":"ATO, Your private health insurance statement, Benefit code","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/private-health-insurance-rebate/your-private-health-insurance-statement","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Benefit code 1","k":"Private health insurance benefit code (30, 31, 35, 36, 40 or 41), policy details line 1","def":"A two-digit code drawn from the insurer's statement, one per line of policy detail, reported by the health fund rather than chosen by the taxpayer. The ATO's instruction for a partner is to \"write the amount of your share of the net small business income at N (do not reduce this amount by any deductions that you are entitled to claim for income tax purposes)\". For a sole trader it is business turnover less the deductions attributable to that turnover; a share received from a partnership or trust is entered at its face value.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label N","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/supplementary-tax-return/tax-offset-questions-t7-t14/t13-entrepreneurs-tax-offset-2012","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Entrepreneurs tax offset net small business entity income","k":"Dollar amount of net small business income reported for the entrepreneurs tax offset","def":"Whole dollars at question T13 label N. Only lodgers with aggregated turnover under $75,000 completed the item, so the column is a truncated, self-selected slice of small business rather than a population measure, and it stops after 2011-12.","where":["madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0607 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0607_16m","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0708 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0708_16m","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0809 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0809_16m"]},{"n":"ENTR_ASMT_STS_TNOVR_AMT","d":"The turnover of the business the entrepreneurs tax offset was claimed on, measured across the whole related group rather than the taxpayer alone.","full":"The turnover of the business the entrepreneurs tax offset was claimed on, measured across the whole related group rather than the taxpayer alone. The ATO defines aggregated turnover as \"your annual turnover for the income year plus the annual turnover of any entity connected or affiliated with you at any time during the income year less income derived from dealings between you and any entity connected or affiliated with you.\" A partner or beneficiary writes the partnership's or trust's turnover here, not their own share of it.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label K","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/supplementary-tax-return/tax-offset-questions-t7-t14/t13-entrepreneurs-tax-offset-2012","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Entrepreneurs tax offset small business entity aggregated turnover","k":"Dollar amount of aggregated turnover reported for the entrepreneurs tax offset","def":"Whole dollars at question T13 label K, excluding GST charged and ordinary income from retail fuel sales, and grossed to a full year estimate where the business operated for only part of the year.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label K","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/supplementary-tax-return/tax-offset-questions-t7-t14/t13-entrepreneurs-tax-offset-2012","lim":"Because a partner writes the entity's turnover rather than a share, adding this column across individuals counts the same business once per partner. The ATO defines it as \"a tax offset equal to 25% of the income tax liability attributable to the net small business income of a small business entity with an aggregated turnover of $50,000 or less\", tapering to nothing at $75,000 of turnover, with a further reduction of 20 cents in the dollar once income passed $70,000 for a single person or $120,000 for someone with a family. The taxpayer did not claim a figure: \"We will automatically calculate your ETO from the information you provide at this item and at other items on your tax return.\"","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/supplementary-tax-return/tax-offset-questions-t7-t14/t13-entrepreneurs-tax-offset-2012","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Entrepreneurs tax offset","k":"Dollar amount of entrepreneurs tax offset allowed at assessment","def":"Whole dollars calculated by the ATO from the turnover and net small business income reported at question T13 together with the rest of the return. It is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or transferred.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/supplementary-tax-return/tax-offset-questions-t7-t14/t13-entrepreneurs-tax-offset-2012","lim":"Because the offset is non-refundable, a zero can mean the person had no tax to reduce rather than no entitlement, so the column measures tax position as well as business size. The offset was abolished from 2012-13, so its disappearance is a change in the law and not a collapse in small business activity.","where":["madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0607 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0607_16m","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0708 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0708_16m","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0809 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0809_16m"]},{"n":"ERLY_RPMTS_NTRL_DSTR_AMT","d":"Farm management deposits a primary producer withdrew inside the normal twelve-month minimum, under the exception for a declared natural disaster or for drought.","full":"Farm management deposits a primary producer withdrew inside the normal twelve-month minimum, under the exception for a declared natural disaster or for drought. The ATO says \"This tax offset is non-refundable, however you can carry it forward if you don't fully utilise it in 2024-25\", and the balance is reported back to the taxpayer on the notice of assessment rather than being written on the return. The ATO instruction is to \"Write the amount of unused early stage investor tax offset to carry forward from the previous year, reduced by any net exempt income, at question T8 – label O.\" The taxpayer has to make the exempt income reduction themselves before writing the figure, so the label is a self-assessed transcription rather than a system-supplied value.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor, label O","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2025/t8-early-stage-investor-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Early stage investor tax offset carried forward from previous year","k":"Dollar amount reported at question T8 label O of the supplementary tax return","def":"Whole dollars at question T8 label O, net of a reduction of 30 cents per dollar of unused net exempt income. The rate applies to the smaller of two figures, because the ATO says \"If you're a limited partner of an ESVCLP, your amount of the tax offset for each contribution in the ESVCLP is 10% of the lesser of the following\": the contribution made during the year, or the investor's share of the eligible venture capital investments the partnership itself made. The ATO instruction is to \"Write the amount of unused ESVCLP tax offset you carry forward from 2023-24, reduced by any net exempt income, at question T7 – label M.\" The reduction is 30 cents in the dollar of unused net exempt income and the taxpayer applies it themselves before writing the figure.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T7 Early stage venture capital limited partnership, label M","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2025/t7-early-stage-venture-capital-limited-partnership-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"ESVCLP offset carried forward from previous year","k":"Dollar amount reported at question T7 label M of the supplementary tax return","def":"Whole dollars at question T7 label M, transcribed from the earlier year's notice of assessment or amended assessment and adjusted for net exempt income.","p":"2020-2021 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T7 Early stage venture capital limited partnership, label M","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2025/t7-early-stage-venture-capital-limited-partnership-2025","lim":"It dates the entitlement to an earlier year, so it cannot be used to place a venture capital contribution in the year the column is populated. The ATO instruction is \"Write at Date of payment the payment date on your income statement or payment summary.\" It is a payment date, not a termination date, and the two can be months apart for a payment made after a dispute or a late settlement.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/4-employment-termination-payments-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Employment Termination Payments - date of payment","k":"Date of an employment termination payment, item 4 of the individual tax return","def":"A calendar date on the individual return at item 4, entered alongside the payer's ABN. The domain is open and there is no code list.","p":"2009-2010","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/4-employment-termination-payments-2025","lim":"It is deliberately left empty for anyone with two or more termination payments, because those are reported on a schedule and the ATO says \"Don't write any date of payment or payer's ABN.\" A missing date therefore signals multiple payments rather than a gap in the data, and treating it as the date employment ended will misdate a late or disputed payment.","where":["madipge-ato-d-context-fy0910 / ato_itr_context_0910_16m"]},{"n":"ETP_OR_LSP_AVLBLOFST_CALCD_AMT","d":"The offset that holds the tax on a termination payment down to a concessional rate, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed by the taxpayer.","full":"The offset that holds the tax on a termination payment down to a concessional rate, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed by the taxpayer. It brings the rate on the taxable component to \"17% if you reach your preservation age\" or 32% if not, and only up to a cap: the ATO says \"Any amount over the relevant cap will be taxed at the top marginal rate of 45% plus Medicare levy of 2%.\" Which cap applies depends on the ETP code, since codes O and P are tested against the whole-of-income cap as well as the ETP cap.","dsrc":"ATO, How ETP components are taxed","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/jobs-and-employment-types/working-as-an-employee/leaving-your-job/how-etp-components-are-taxed","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Termination payment tax offset","k":"Dollar amount of employment termination payment tax offset calculated at assessment","def":"Whole dollars derived at assessment as the difference between tax at the taxpayer's marginal rate and tax at the capped concessional rate on the taxable component. It also carries no information about why the payment was made, which lives in the ETP code on the same row.","where":["madip-ge-020105d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1011","madip-ge-020110d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1112","madip-ge-020115d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1213","madip-ge-020120d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1314","madip-ge-020125d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1415","madip-ge-020130d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1516","madip-ge-020135d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1617","madip-ge-020140d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1718","madip-ge-020140d-ato-atoitrwhlddebt1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_whld_debt_1819","madipge-ato-d-whld-debt-fy0001 / ato_itr_whld_debt_0001","madipge-ato-d-whld-debt-fy0102 / ato_itr_whld_debt_0102","madipge-ato-d-whld-debt-fy0203 / ato_itr_whld_debt_0203","and 11 more"]},{"n":"ETP_TYP_CD","d":"A single letter saying why the termination payment was made, which then decides how much of it is taxed concessionally.","full":"A single letter saying why the termination payment was made, which then decides how much of it is taxed concessionally. R covers redundancy, early retirement, invalidity and compensation for personal injury, unfair dismissal, harassment or discrimination; O covers everything else, such as a golden handshake or payment in lieu of notice; S and P mark a second payment for the same termination; D, B and N mark death benefit payments by the recipient's dependency status; and T marks a payment to the trustee of a deceased estate. The taxpayer copies the letter rather than choosing it: \"You must enter a valid code, find it on your income statement or payment summary.\" The distinction is not cosmetic, because the ATO's page on how ETP components are taxed says a payment \"is subject to the whole-of-income cap, if the code on your end of year statement is O or P\".","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code descriptions; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/4-employment-termination-payments-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Type of taxable employment termination payment","k":"ETP code at item 4 of the individual tax return (R, O, S, P, D, B, N, T, M)","def":"A one-character code taken from the payer's income statement or payment summary. Code M is used instead where the taxpayer received two or more ETPs and lodged an employment termination payment schedule.","p":"2009-2010 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code descriptions; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/4-employment-termination-payments-2025","lim":"For exactly the people with several termination payments the reason is lost, because code M replaces the substantive codes and the schedule is not carried here. The code is also chosen by the payer, so a redundancy coded O rather than R reflects the employer's judgement and not the character of the payment.","where":["madip-ge-020102d-ato-atoitrcontext1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_context_1011","madip-ge-020107d-ato-atoitrcontext1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_context_1112","madip-ge-020112d-ato-atoitrcontext1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_context_1213","madip-ge-020117d-ato-atoitrcontext1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_context_1314","madip-ge-020122d-ato-atoitrcontext1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_context_1415","madip-ge-020127d-ato-atoitrcontext1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_context_1516","madip-ge-020132d-ato-atoitrcontext1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_context_1617","madip-ge-020137d-ato-atoitrcontext1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_context_1718","madip-ge-020137d-ato-atoitrcontext1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_context_1819","madipge-ato-d-context-fy0910 / ato_itr_context_0910_16m","madipge-ato-d-context-fy1920 / ato_itr_context_1920","madipge-ato-d-context-fy1920 / ato_itr_context_1920_16m","and 5 more"]},{"n":"ETPS_EXCSVCMPNT_AMT","d":"The part of a 2006-07 termination payment that took the person past their lifetime concessional limit and so lost every concession.","full":"The part of a 2006-07 termination payment that took the person past their lifetime concessional limit and so lost every concession. Under the pre-2007 regime each person had a reasonable benefit limit, which the ATO describes as being used \"to determine the concessional tax rates limits of a reasonable benefit limit (RBL) for a particular financial year\", covering both pension and lump sum benefits. Anything above that limit was the excessive component and was taxed at the top rate, which is why the return reported it apart from the rest of the payment.","dsrc":"ATO, Other super rates and thresholds, Reasonable benefit limits","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/key-superannuation-rates-and-thresholds/other-super-rates-and-thresholds","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Employment termination payments - excessive component’","k":"Dollar amount, excessive component of an eligible termination payment, to 30 June 2007","def":"Whole dollars on the 2006-07 individual return, reported separately from the balance of the payment, which the column names on the same row describe as the amount other than the excessive component.","p":"2006-2007","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Other super rates and thresholds, Reasonable benefit limits","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/key-superannuation-rates-and-thresholds/other-super-rates-and-thresholds","lim":"Reasonable benefit limits were abolished from 1 July 2007, so the column empties out after 2006-07 and that break is a change in the law rather than a change in redundancy behaviour. It is also not comparable with the ETP cap that replaced it, since a reasonable benefit limit was a lifetime measure across a person's whole benefits and the cap applies payment by payment.","where":["madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0607 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0607_16m"]},{"n":"ETPS_OTHRTHN_EXCSVCMPNT_AMT","d":"The assessable part of a termination payment, being what is left once the tax-free amount is stripped out.","full":"The assessable part of a termination payment, being what is left once the tax-free amount is stripped out. The instruction is to \"Write the taxable component of your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary at question 4 – label I\", and the ATO's page on ETP components explains that \"After any tax-free amount is deducted from your payment, the balance is the taxable component\". The column name preserves the older framing of an amount other than the excessive component, from the reasonable benefit limit regime that no longer applies, but the quantity reported is the taxable component at item 4 label I.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, label I; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/4-employment-termination-payments-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Employment termination payments taxable component","k":"Dollar amount, taxable component of employment termination payments, item 4 label I","def":"Whole dollars taken from the payer's income statement or payment summary and written at item 4 label I. If it was 91 days or more, your foreign employment income will generally be exempt from tax.\" The exemption is narrow, reaching relief work financed from a declared developing country relief fund, employment by a prescribed charitable or religious institution, deployment as a member of an Australian Government disciplined force and Austrade-approved projects, rather than expatriate employment generally.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/20-foreign-source-income-and-foreign-assets-or-property-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Foreign source income exempt foreign employment income","k":"Dollar amount of exempt foreign employment income, item 20 label N","def":"Whole dollars at item 20 label N, converted to Australian currency and reduced by the non-capital expenses of earning the income, with a loss written as zero.","p":"2006-2007 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/20-foreign-source-income-and-foreign-assets-or-property-2025","lim":"It is not a measure of overseas work: a posting of 90 days or less produces nothing here even though the income was foreign and the person was abroad, and taxable foreign employment income goes to item 20 label U instead. Income tax returns keep changing after the year closes, as returns are lodged late, amended and audited, so the same income year extracted at two dates is two different datasets. The suffix on the table name is that lag: ato_itr_context_2021_16m is the 2020-21 year as it stood sixteen months after the year ended. Comparing across years means comparing like lags rather than like income years.","dsrc":"ABS administrative income sources","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/concepts-sources-methods/administrative-income-comparison-studies/2019-20-2021","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"ATO data extract time","k":"ATO extract reference date","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2018-2019 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS administrative income sources","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/concepts-sources-methods/administrative-income-comparison-studies/2019-20-2021","lim":"The column describes the extract, not the person, so it is never an analysis variable. The ATO says \"You don't include in your assessable income any part of a distribution to you on which family trust distribution tax has already been paid\", so the money never reaches taxable income. It is collected anyway because the Medicare levy surcharge test adds it back, and a spouse copies it into the spouse income section of their own return.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item A5","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/a5-amount-you-paid-family-trust-distribution-tax-on-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid","k":"Dollar amount reported at tax return item A5 label X","def":"A whole-dollar amount, being the distributions that would have been assessable less any expenses that would have been deductible against them. The ATO instruction is to \"Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 – label Q.\" The claim only stands where the matching franked distribution is at label O, U or C on the same row, and where the holding period and related payments rules are satisfied.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/13-partnerships-and-trusts-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Share of franking credit from franked dividends","k":"Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 13 label Q","def":"A dollars-and-cents amount, self-assessed from the distribution statement the partnership or trust issued, covering imputation credits received indirectly only.","p":"2006-2007 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/13-partnerships-and-trusts-2025","lim":"It is the credit claimed rather than the credit the trust or partnership was entitled to pass on, and a trust in overall tax loss passes on none at all. The ATO now states flatly that \"The FIF measures have been repealed and do not apply to taxpayers from 2010–11.\" Until then Part XI of the ITAA 1936 taxed Australian residents on income accumulating inside a foreign company or trust they did not control, whether or not any of it was paid out. The column appears only in the 2009-10 extract for that reason.","dsrc":"ATO, Foreign income return form guide, chapter 4","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/foreign-income-return-form-guide/chapter-4-taxation-of-foreign-investment-fund-fif-interests","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"FIF and FLP income","k":"Dollar amount of attributed foreign investment fund and foreign life policy income (income years to 2009-10)","def":"A whole-dollar accruals amount worked out under Part XI of the ITAA 1936 and reported in the foreign entities item of the supplementary return. The ATO instruction is to \"Write the number of your dependent children (from worksheet 2 – row e ) at question M1 – label Y . If you have none, write 0 (zero).\" A dependent child must be an Australian resident the person maintained and must fall under the adjusted taxable income limits for the year. The ATO scopes item 1 as income \"from salary or wages where tax was withheld\", which takes in commissions, bonuses, part-time and casual work, parental leave pay, and lost-wage payments under income protection, sickness and accident or workers compensation arrangements. Allowances are excluded and belong at item 2. The label is a calculated total, so it aggregates the payer rows rather than naming one employer.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 1","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/1-salary-or-wages-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Salary or wages","k":"Dollar amount reported at tax return item 1, Income column","def":"A whole-dollar total across payers, self-assessed but assembled from employer-reported income statements that the ATO pre-fills.","p":"1999-2000, 2000-2001, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004, 2004-2005, 2005-2006, 2009-2010, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 1","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/1-salary-or-wages-2025","lim":"It is not total employment income: allowances, employment termination payments, employer lump sums and any business or personal services income are separate items, and amounts salary sacrificed to superannuation never appear anywhere on the return. The ATO defines the pair of labels as \"the total income you receive, from which your payers have withheld tax because you didn't quote your ABN\", and label D is the non-primary production half. The taxpayer builds it from the payment summary schedule rows typed N. Completing the label obliges the person to claim the matching credit at item 15 label W.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments where ABN not quoted - non-primary production","k":"Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label D","def":"A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of the tax withheld, built by adding payment summary schedule rows typed N that came from non-primary production activities.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"A non-zero value marks a registration or paperwork failure rather than a level of activity, so it cannot be read as a measure of contracting income. It also cannot say whether the person had no ABN at all or simply failed to quote one on that job.","where":["madip-ge-020104d-ato-atoitrincloss1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1011","madip-ge-020109d-ato-atoitrincloss1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1112","madip-ge-020114d-ato-atoitrincloss1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1213","madip-ge-020119d-ato-atoitrincloss1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1314","madip-ge-020124d-ato-atoitrincloss1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1415","madip-ge-020129d-ato-atoitrincloss1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1516","madip-ge-020134d-ato-atoitrincloss1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1617","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1718","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1819","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0607 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0607_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0708 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0708_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0809 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0809_16m","and 7 more"]},{"n":"GRS_PMTS_ABN_NOT_QTD_PP_AMT","d":"Farming, fishing or forestry income the sole trader received from payers who withheld tax because no ABN was quoted.","full":"Farming, fishing or forestry income the sole trader received from payers who withheld tax because no ABN was quoted. The taxpayer builds it by adding \"all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule, derived from primary production activities that have an N in the Type box.\" The split from the non-primary production half matters because primary production income runs through separate averaging and farm concession rules later in the assessment.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments where ABN not quoted - primary production","k":"Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label C","def":"A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of withheld tax, covering primary production activities only.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"The primary production tag comes from the taxpayer's own classification of the activity when they fill in the payment summary schedule, not from the payer, so the split against the non-primary production column is self-assessed. It is the totals box of the pair: the ATO says to \"Add up the amounts you have written at labels C and D and enter the total in the adjacent Totals box.\" Reaching this label at all means a payer had to withhold at source, and the ATO then requires the person to claim the matching credit at item 15 label W in the supplementary return.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments where abn not quoted - total","k":"Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income, ABN not quoted totals box","def":"A whole-dollar gross total covering both the primary production and non-primary production ABN-not-quoted labels on the same row, inclusive of the tax withheld.","p":"2010-2011 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"Because it is the sum of the two columns beside it, using all three together counts the same dollars three times. It is the working half of the pair, because the ATO expects nothing in the primary production box: \"It is expected you'll not have any primary production amounts at this question. Leave P8 Income – label N blank.\" Income earned as an employee of a labour hire business belongs at item 1 instead, not here.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments - labour hire or other specified payments - non-primary production","k":"Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label O","def":"A whole-dollar gross amount including the tax withheld, built by adding all payment summary schedule rows typed S.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"It captures only non-employee labour hire work, so an agency worker treated as an employee has the same job recorded as salary at item 1 and this column is not a measure of labour hire employment. Leave P8 Income – label N blank.\" The column exists because the schedule prints a primary production and a non-primary production box on every income row, not because the payment types arise in agriculture.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments - labour hire or other specified payments - primary production","k":"Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label N","def":"A whole-dollar gross amount that mirrors the non-primary production labour hire label but is left blank by design on the ATO's own instruction.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"A non-zero value is more likely a form-filling error than a distinct kind of income, so it should not be read as agricultural labour hire. The ATO defines it as follows: \"The amount you show at label B is the total income you receive from your payers that is subject to foreign resident withholding. It includes any amounts of tax withheld.\" Foreign resident capital gains withholding is deliberately excluded and goes to item 18. The column appears in the 2006-07 extract with a handful of occurrences and does not carry forward, so it reads as an artefact of the older form layout.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments subject to foreign resident withholding - primary production","k":"Dollar amount reported in the primary production column of the P8 foreign resident withholding income row","def":"A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of withheld tax, present only in the earliest extract vintage and paired with the non-primary production column on the same row.","p":"2006-2007, 2008-2009","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"With so few occurrences the column cannot support a rate, a share or a trend, and a single unusual return would dominate any statistic built from it. The ATO defines the pair as \"the total income you receive that is subject to a voluntary agreement to withhold tax and include the tax withheld\", and label F is the non-primary production half. The ATO's own arithmetic for individuals starts from this figure: \"Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax − Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge − Remaining foreign income tax offset\". Gross tax is the first term, so the gap between it and net tax is the entire offset and levy structure. The ATO calculates it from the return rather than the taxpayer entering it.","dsrc":"ATO, Reference material for Taxation statistics 2023-24, Calculating net tax","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/research-and-statistics/in-detail/taxation-statistics/taxation-statistics-2023-24/reference-material-for-taxation-statistics-2023-24","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Gross tax","k":"Dollar amount of tax on taxable income before offsets","def":"A whole-dollar amount produced by applying the resident or foreign resident rate scale for that income year to taxable income, together with any extra income tax.","p":"1999-2000, 2000-2001, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004, 2004-2005, 2005-2006, 2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Reference material for Taxation statistics 2023-24, Calculating net tax","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/research-and-statistics/in-detail/taxation-statistics/taxation-statistics-2023-24/reference-material-for-taxation-statistics-2023-24","lim":"It is not what the person paid: offsets, the Medicare levy, the surcharge and withholding credits all sit between this and the assessment outcome, so someone with a large gross tax can still finish the year with a refund. It is the totals box of the pair: \"Add up the amounts you show at P8 Income – labels E and F , and write the total in the adjacent Totals box.\" The figure is gross of the tax withheld, and the person claims the withheld amount back at item 15 label D on the supplementary return.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross payments - voluntary agreement - total","k":"Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income, voluntary agreement totals box","def":"A whole-dollar gross total combining the primary production and non-primary production voluntary agreement labels on the same row.","p":"2010-2011 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/income-p8","lim":"It is the sum of the two columns beside it, so using all three together counts the same dollars repeatedly. The return records dates rather than a count: if the person did not have a spouse for the full year they \"print X in the No box at label L and write the dates you have a spouse in 2024–25 at labels M and N.\" This column carries the length of that period. Spouse covers married, registered and de facto relationships alike.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/spouse-details-married-or-defacto-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Part-year spouse days","k":"Number of days with a spouse in the income year","def":"A day count derived from the from and to dates at labels M and N, bounded by the 1 July to 30 June income year.","p":"2009-2010 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/spouse-details-married-or-defacto-2025","lim":"Only the last spouse of the year is described, so a person with two relationships in one year has the earlier one hidden entirely. The instruction is direct: \"If you have a spouse for the full income year, 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025, print X in the Yes box at label L.\" A no sends the person to the date labels on the same row. The ATO uses the answer with spouse income to work out the private health insurance rebate, the seniors and pensioners tax offset, any Medicare levy reduction and the Medicare levy surcharge.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/spouse-details-married-or-defacto-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Did you have a spouse for the full year?","k":"Yes or no indicator reported at tax return spouse details label L","def":"A single flag for a full-year spouse relationship, covering married, registered and de facto partners under the ATO's definition.","p":"2009-2010 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/spouse-details-married-or-defacto-2025","lim":"It is not a partnership status variable for the whole population: a person with no spouse at any time leaves the entire section blank, so blanks mix single people with people who simply did not complete it. The ATO definition turns on a registered relationship or living together on a genuine domestic basis, which will not always match how a household survey would classify the same couple.","where":["madip-ge-020102d-ato-atoitrcontext1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_context_1011","madip-ge-020107d-ato-atoitrcontext1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_context_1112","madip-ge-020112d-ato-atoitrcontext1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_context_1213","madip-ge-020117d-ato-atoitrcontext1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_context_1314","madip-ge-020122d-ato-atoitrcontext1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_context_1415","madip-ge-020127d-ato-atoitrcontext1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_context_1516","madip-ge-020132d-ato-atoitrcontext1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_context_1617","madip-ge-020137d-ato-atoitrcontext1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_context_1718","madip-ge-020137d-ato-atoitrcontext1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_context_1819","madipge-ato-d-context-fy0910 / ato_itr_context_0910_16m","madipge-ato-d-context-fy1920 / ato_itr_context_1920","madipge-ato-d-context-fy1920 / ato_itr_context_1920_16m","and 5 more"]},{"n":"HE_LOAN_PGMME_RPMT_DUE_AMT","d":"The compulsory study and training loan repayment the ATO raised on the person's assessment for that year.","full":"The compulsory study and training loan repayment the ATO raised on the person's assessment for that year. The taxpayer does not work it out: \"If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.\" Repayment income is wider than taxable income, adding reportable fringe benefits and total net investment loss.","dsrc":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Australian help assessment debt","k":"Dollar amount of compulsory study and training loan repayment raised on the assessment","def":"A whole-dollar amount computed by the ATO from repayment income against the thresholds and rates for that income year, and added to the assessment rather than reported on the return.","p":"2010-2011 to 2014-2015","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","lim":"It is not what the person paid across the year: employers withhold extra amounts against the loan through pay as you go, and those withholdings appear as tax withheld rather than here. The column name expands to higher education loan programme collectable debt outstanding amount. It is an ATO account balance rather than anything the taxpayer writes on the return, and it does not move with each pay: \"Your loan balance doesn't reduce after each pay cycle; it is only applied as a lump sum after your income tax return is lodged.\"","dsrc":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"HECS accumulation debt amount","k":"Dollar amount of outstanding collectable study and training loan debt","def":"A whole-dollar balance held on the person's ATO loan account, reduced by compulsory repayments applied after lodgement and by any voluntary repayments.","p":"2010-2011 to 2014-2015","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","lim":"It is an account balance rather than borrowing for the year, so it cannot tell you when or how much the person borrowed. Voluntary repayments are additional to the compulsory one and \"will not impact your compulsory repayment\" while a balance remains and repayment income is above the threshold, so paying extra reduces the balance without reducing the amount raised on the assessment. Several columns in these extracts describe a loan balance and the custodian's wording repeats across them.","dsrc":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"HECS accumulation debt amount","k":"Dollar amount of outstanding repayable study and training loan balance (2017-18 extract)","def":"A whole-dollar loan account balance for one extract vintage, held by the ATO rather than reported by the taxpayer.","p":"2017-2018 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","lim":"More than one column in these extracts carries the identical custodian's description, so matching on that description instead of the column name will merge quantities that are not the same. The compulsory repayment is worked out against this balance and stops when the balance clears; the threshold has since moved, and \"From the 2025–26 income year, you only need to make a compulsory repayment when your repayment income exceeds $67,000\", calculated only on income above that point. The column is a later name for the outstanding balance rather than a new quantity.","dsrc":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"HELP Repayable Debt","k":"Dollar amount of repayable HELP debt (2020-21 extract)","def":"A whole-dollar loan balance held by the ATO, carried alongside the compulsory repayment amount for the year in the same extracts.","p":"2020-2021 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Compulsory repayments","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/study-and-training-support-loans/compulsory-repayments","lim":"The repayable balance and the compulsory repayment for the year are different quantities and both appear in these extracts, so using this column as a repayment measure overstates by an order of magnitude. It is a calculated figure, not a claim: the ATO says that from 2025-26 \"your compulsory repayment is calculated only on the income above the minimum repayment threshold\". The word maximum in the label reads as the amount before it is trimmed to whatever the person still owes, so it can exceed the repayment actually raised. The ATO defines it as follows: \"Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution.\" It counts twice on the return, once as assessable income and once as a credit: \"You also receive a tax credit on your tax assessment for an amount equal to the franking credits.\"","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/11-dividends-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Imputation Credit Amount","k":"Franking credit amount at question 11 label U (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount taken from dividend statements, added to the franked and unfranked dividend labels on the same row and also carried to the credits side of the assessment.","p":"1999-2000 to 2005-2006","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/11-dividends-2025","lim":"It is not a payment the person received, so treating it as cash income overstates their means, and treating it as tax paid by them attributes a company's tax to a household. The individual non-business payment summary is the form an employer gives to \"workers or payees who are employees, company directors or office holders\", and it carries pensions and annuities, Commonwealth benefits and allowances, compensation and sickness payments and working holiday maker earnings alongside ordinary salary. Treating every row on this form as wages counts pensions and benefits as employment income.","dsrc":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Individual non-business income type","k":"Individual non-business income type","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business","lim":"The ATO publishes the form but not the codes PLIDA uses for the income type, so the mapping is not confirmed. The distinctions this column carries are precisely the ones that matter for measuring employment, so the gap is a real constraint.","where":["madipge-ato-d-pay-sum-fy2324 / plida_ps_2324_12m_bn"]},{"n":"INCM_IDV_TXBL_SB_AMT","d":"The part of the person's taxable income the ATO attributed to unincorporated small business, used to work out their small business income tax offset.","full":"The part of the person's taxable income the ATO attributed to unincorporated small business, used to work out their small business income tax offset. The ATO describes the mechanism as follows: \"The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income\", built from sole trader net small business income plus any share from a small business partnership or trust. The proportion is capped at one, so this amount never exceeds taxable income on the same row.","dsrc":"ATO, Small business income tax offset","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-income-tax-offset","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Small business proportion of taxable income","k":"Small business share of taxable income used for the offset (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount derived by the ATO from the return, not a label the taxpayer fills in. It is net of business deductions, excludes salary, wages and net capital gains, and is treated as zero when the business made a loss.","p":"2015-2016 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Small business income tax offset","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-income-tax-offset","lim":"It is a calculation input, not income the person can spend, and it is not added to taxable income anywhere. It also exists only for years and turnovers in which the offset ran, so a blank can mean an ineligible business rather than none: the turnover threshold was $2 million in 2015-16 before rising to $5 million.","where":["madip-ge-020129d-ato-atoitrincloss1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1516","madip-ge-020134d-ato-atoitrincloss1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1617","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1718","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1819","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy1920 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1920","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy1920 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1920_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2021 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2021_12m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2021 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2021_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2021-22 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2122_12m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2223 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2223_12m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2324 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2324_12m"]},{"n":"INCM_OR_LSS_TOTL_AMT","d":"Everything the taxpayer declared as income for the year, added up before any deduction is taken off.","full":"Everything the taxpayer declared as income for the year, added up before any deduction is taken off. The return works down from it: the ATO says to \"subtract the amount at Total deductions from the amount at Total income or loss\" and write the result at Subtotal, which after earlier-year losses becomes taxable income. It gathers the twelve income questions on the main return and the supplement total on the same row.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Subtotal","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/deduction-questions-d1-d10-individual-tax-return-2025/subtotal-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total income or loss","k":"Total income or loss on the return (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, the sum of the income labels across the main return and the supplement, which can be negative and is then flagged as a loss.","p":"1999-2000 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Subtotal","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/deduction-questions-d1-d10-individual-tax-return-2025/subtotal-2025","lim":"It is a gross figure, so it is not a measure of what the household kept: a sole trader with $400,000 of turnover-driven income and $390,000 of deductions looks wealthy here and poor at taxable income. The ATO puts the arithmetic simply: \"Your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions.\" Add-backs are assessable amounts missing from the accounts, such as balancing adjustments on asset disposals; subtractions are book income that is exempt or not assessable. The figure is the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns and can be negative.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/reconciliation-items","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Income reconciliation adjustments - total","k":"Income reconciliation adjustment at P8 label X (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, signed, that is the net of add-backs and subtractions across both production columns. The ATO builds it by adding \"all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24\" and subtracting the losses from partnerships and trusts, farm deposits, foreign income and rent. It is then carried to label I on the main return, which is where it joins wages, interest and dividends in total income or loss.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/total-supplement-income-or-loss-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total supplement income or loss","k":"Total supplement income or loss (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, signed, that nets the supplement's income and loss questions. It is present only where the person lodged a supplementary return.","p":"2009-2010 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/total-supplement-income-or-loss-2025","lim":"It is a mixed bag rather than a category: business, rent, capital gains, foreign income and one-off other income all land in the one number, so a change in it cannot be read as a change in any of them. A blank means no supplement was lodged, not that the person had no investments.","where":["madip-ge-020104d-ato-atoitrincloss1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1011","madip-ge-020109d-ato-atoitrincloss1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1112","madip-ge-020114d-ato-atoitrincloss1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1213","madip-ge-020119d-ato-atoitrincloss1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1314","madip-ge-020124d-ato-atoitrincloss1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1415","madip-ge-020129d-ato-atoitrincloss1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1516","madip-ge-020134d-ato-atoitrincloss1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1617","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1718","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1819","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0910 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0910_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy1920 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1920","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy1920 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1920_16m","and 5 more"]},{"n":"INCM_TYP_CD","d":"The income type the employer assigned to the payments on this row when reporting them through Single Touch Payroll.","full":"The income type the employer assigned to the payments on this row when reporting them through Single Touch Payroll. The ATO makes the residual nature of the main code plain: \"If the payments you are making to your employee don't belong in one of the other specific income types, use the SAW income type.\" The table holds one row per payer per year, with ABN_HASH_TRUNC naming the employer and SW_GRS_PMT_AMT and SW_TW_AMT carrying the amounts.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, 'Income types'","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/income-types","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Income type","k":"ato_stp_income_type","def":"Three letter codes: SAW, CHP, WHM, FEI, IAA, SWP, JPD, VOL, LAB and OSP. VOL and LAB rows are contractor payments rather than employment, and one payer reporting two income types for a person creates two rows, so counting rows here does not count jobs.","where":["madipge-ato-d-wages-salaries-fy1819 / ato_wages_salaries_1819_16m","madipge-ato-d-wages-salaries-fy1920 / ato_wages_salaries_1920_16m","madipge-ato-d-wages-salaries-fy2021 / ato_wages_salaries_2021_16m","madipge-ato-d-ws-fy2021-22 / ato_ws_2122_12m","madipge-ato-d-ws-fy2021-22 / ato_ws_2122_16m","madipge-ato-d-ws-fy2022-23 / ato_ws_2223_12m","madipge-ato-d-ws-fy2324 / plida_itr_ws_2324_12m_bn"],"dom":6},{"n":"INCM_YR","d":"The financial year the return reports on, which for individuals runs from 1 July to 30 June.","full":"The financial year the return reports on, which for individuals runs from 1 July to 30 June. The ATO's own definition allows for exceptions: an income year \"is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act\". It is the year the income was earned, not the year the return was lodged or assessed.","dsrc":"ATO, Foreign income return form guide, glossary entry Income year","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/foreign-income-return-form-guide-2005/glossary/income-year","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Income year","k":"Financial year of the return (income year)","def":"A year identifier for a 1 July to 30 June period, usually stored as the ending year or as a paired label such as 2010-11.","p":"1999-2000 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Foreign income return form guide, glossary entry Income year","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/foreign-income-return-form-guide-2005/glossary/income-year","lim":"It is not a lodgment date and not a payment date, so a return for an early year can be lodged years late and still carry that year here. The ATO drew the line at transacting rather than having a web presence: you tick no if you used the internet only to \"advertise your goods or services, give support to your customers, buy your stock, do your banking\". The question ran on the individual, partnership and trust returns and was dropped from the schedule in later years.","dsrc":"ATO, Trust tax return instructions 2014, question 4 Did you sell any goods or services using the internet?","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/trust-tax-return-2014-instructions/remainder-of-trust-tax-return/4-did-you-sell-any-goods-or-services-using-the-internet","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Did you sell any goods or services using the internet","k":"Yes or no answer on internet selling","def":"A two-state self-assessed indicator. The cited wording is the trust return's version of the identically worded question, because the individual schedule's own page has been retired from the ATO site.","p":"1999-2000, 2000-2001, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004, 2004-2005, 2005-2006, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Trust tax return instructions 2014, question 4 Did you sell any goods or services using the internet?","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/trust-tax-return-2014-instructions/remainder-of-trust-tax-return/4-did-you-sell-any-goods-or-services-using-the-internet","lim":"It is a yes-or-no about method, so it measures neither how much was sold online nor whether the business had a website; a shop taking one order by email answers the same as a full online retailer. The ATO ties the claim to the income it produced: \"To claim a deduction for interest income expenses, you must incur expenses in earning interest from any source in Australia.\" Deductions against dividends go to the next question instead, and interest costs inside a business, a rental property or a trust distribution are claimed elsewhere again.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D7 Interest income deductions","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/deduction-questions-d1-d10-individual-tax-return-2025/d7-interest-income-deductions-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Interest deductions","k":"Interest deductions claimed at question D7 (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount claimed against the gross interest label on the same return. The current return splits the same ground across two questions, D7 for interest income deductions and D8 for dividend deductions, and the ATO's apportionment rule shows they are treated as one pool of investment cost: a shared computer's decline in value is claimed \"once, at either question D7 or D8\". The schedule keeps two columns and one total: \"Add up your primary production and non-primary production overseas interest expenses and write the total at label R.\" It is deliberately separated from interest paid within Australia, which sits in its own label on the same schedule, because overseas interest carries withholding and thin capitalisation consequences.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/expenses-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Interest expenses overseas - total","k":"Overseas interest expenses at P8, total column (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount for the income year, the sum of the two production columns on the expenses page of the schedule. It sits opposite the employment and business income label, and the pair decide whether at least 10% of total income came from work.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/adjustment-questions-a1-a4-individual-tax-return-2025/a3-government-super-contributions-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Government super contributions income from investment partnership and other sources","k":"Income from investment, partnership and other sources at question A3 label F (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount assembled from worksheets rather than transcribed from a single label, covering the investment and other income components of total income for co-contribution purposes.","p":"2009-2010 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/adjustment-questions-a1-a4-individual-tax-return-2025/a3-government-super-contributions-2025","lim":"It is not a component of taxable income and does not appear in the assessment, so adding it to income labels elsewhere on the return double counts. The ATO caps what comes out of it: \"Your offset will be your rate of offset of the following amount, up to the limit of $1,000.\" It is the tax counterpart of the small business share of taxable income on the same row, and the offset rate applied to it rose from 5% in 2015-16 to 16% from 2021-22.","dsrc":"ATO, Small business income tax offset","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-income-tax-offset","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Small business proportion of tax liability","k":"Small business share of income tax liability used for the offset (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount of tax, derived by the ATO from the return by multiplying basic income tax liability by the small business proportion, which is capped at one.","p":"2015-2016 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Small business income tax offset","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/income-and-deductions-for-business/concessions-offsets-and-rebates/small-business-income-tax-offset","lim":"It is not the tax the person actually paid on their business, because the offset itself, other offsets, the Medicare levy and loan repayments all sit outside it. The ATO defines the line as follows: \"Total tax withheld is the pay as you go (PAYG) withholding amounts withheld during the year by the payer from the amounts you declare as income at questions 1 to 9.\" It is a credit against the assessment rather than a tax, so a refund is the gap between it and the tax finally worked out.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax withheld","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/total-tax-withheld-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total tax withheld","k":"Total PAYG tax withheld reported on the return (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, the sum of the withheld column beside the first nine income questions. It covers wages, allowances, lump sums, termination payments, government payments and annuities.","p":"2006-2007 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax withheld","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-1-12-individual-tax-return-2025/total-tax-withheld-2025","lim":"It is not the person's tax for the year, and it is not the whole of what they remitted: PAYG instalments are credited separately and are explicitly kept off the return, and withholding on interest or dividends for a missing tax file number sits at those questions. The ATO combines four things in the label: \"Add up your primary production and non-primary production deductions for landcare operations, water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets and write the total at label W.\" Landcare covers works such as levees, drainage and fencing to keep stock off degraded land, and it is deductible in the year it is incurred where the business is a primary producer.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/reconciliation-items","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Landcare operations and business deduction for decline in value of water facility - total","k":"Landcare, water facility, fencing and fodder storage deduction at P8 label W (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns. Fencing and fodder storage components are available to primary producers only; landcare and water facilities can also reach a rural land irrigation water provider.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/reconciliation-items","lim":"The four components cannot be told apart in the one figure, so it cannot be used to measure water infrastructure spending on its own. The ATO draws a boundary that matters for anyone reading the figure as equipment finance: \"Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses.\" Hire purchase is dealt with in the reconciliation labels instead, and a lease can also be caught by the thin capitalisation debt deduction rules.","dsrc":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/expenses-p8","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Lease expenses - total","k":"Lease expenses at P8, total column (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, the sum of the two production columns for lease payments claimed in the accounts.","p":"2006-2007, 2007-2008, 2008-2009, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/business-and-professional-items-schedule-2025-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-bpi-schedule-2025/business-income-and-expenses-p8/expenses-p8","lim":"It cannot separate a property lease from a car or equipment lease, so it is not a measure of business premises cost. The rule is fixed and the calculation is not the taxpayer's: \"You'll get a tax offset equal to 30% of the amount you show at this question. We'll work out this tax offset for you.\" The 30% matches the tax the life company has already paid on the earnings inside the policy, so the offset is there to stop the same income being taxed twice.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/22-life-insurance-companies-and-friendly-societies-bonuses-2025","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Life assurance bonus tax offset","k":"Life assurance bonus tax offset (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount equal to 30% of the assessable bonus reported at question 22, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed.","p":"2010-2011 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2025-instructions/income-questions-13-24-supplementary-tax-return-2025/22-life-insurance-companies-and-friendly-societies-bonuses-2025","lim":"It is a non-refundable offset, so a person with little tax payable does not receive the full 30% as cash, and the recorded amount can therefore overstate the benefit.
