The legacy item name points at payments that were reported as dollar amounts at a different return item, so the column is neither a receipt flag nor an amount.","where":["madipge-ato-d-context-fy9900 / ato_itr_context_9900"]},{"n":"UNPLMT_SKNS_BNFT_AMT","d":"Taxable Australian Government allowances the taxpayer received, reported at label A of item 5 on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06.","full":"Taxable Australian Government allowances the taxpayer received, reported at label A of item 5 on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. TaxPack's list for the item runs to Newstart allowance, youth allowance, sickness allowance, special benefit, partner allowance, widow allowance, austudy payment, mature age allowance, additional parenting payment (partnered), exceptional circumstances relief payment, ABSTUDY living allowance and other taxable Commonwealth education or training payments. Age and service pensions are a different item, so this column is the allowance side of the payment system rather than the pension side. The beneficiary rebate worksheet in the same publication points back to it as \"Total amount of allowance or payment you received-from A item 5 on your tax return\". The column's name survives from the older unemployment and sickness benefit terminology.","dsrc":"ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), question 5","durl":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=0976-6.2000","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Unemployment Sickness Benefit Amount","k":"Dollar amount at label A, item 5 Australian Government allowances and payments, pre-2006 returns","def":"A whole-dollar total of taxable allowance income for the year, taken from Centrelink group certificates or payment summaries and totalled by the taxpayer at one label.","p":"1999-2000 to 2005-2006","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), question 5","url":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=0976-6.2000","lim":"Exempt payments are missing entirely, so the column is not a measure of income support received: a taxpayer whose payment was exempt, or who did not have to lodge, shows nothing. It also cannot separate the payment types inside it, so unemployment, study and caring payments are one figure, and the amount is annual so it says nothing about how many fortnights were paid.","where":["madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0001 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0001","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0102 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0102","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0203 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0203","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0304 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0304","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0405 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0405","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0506 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0506","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy9900 / ato_itr_inc_loss_9900"]},{"n":"UNPLMT_SKNS_BNFT_RBT_AMT","d":"The beneficiary rebate the ATO worked out on the taxpayer's Australian Government allowances, held on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06.","full":"The beneficiary rebate the ATO worked out on the taxpayer's Australian Government allowances, held on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. TaxPack sets out the calculation from the allowance amount at label A of item 5, taking the tax-free threshold off it and applying 20 per cent, with an extra 14 per cent above a higher threshold, and is explicit that the taxpayer does not enter it: \"Do not write your rebate anywhere on your tax return.\" The rebate exists so that a person living on allowance income pays no tax on it. It is therefore a derived amount on the same row as the allowance that generated it.","dsrc":"ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), Beneficiary rebate worksheet","durl":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=0976-6.2000","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Unemployment Sickness Benefit Rebate Amount","k":"Dollar amount of the beneficiary rebate worked out in the assessment, pre-2006 returns","def":"A dollar amount computed by the ATO as a function of the allowance amount at item 5 and the taxpayer's tax-free threshold, not a taxpayer entry.","p":"1999-2000 to 2005-2006","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), Beneficiary rebate worksheet","url":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=0976-6.2000","lim":"It is not evidence of anything the taxpayer claimed, so it should not be read as take-up of a concession. As a non-refundable rebate it is also capped by tax payable, which means a taxpayer on allowances alone can show a rebate that exceeds the tax it could ever offset. Movements in this column track the allowance amount and the threshold rules rather than any change in behaviour.","where":["madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0001 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0001","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0102 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0102","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0203 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0203","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0304 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0304","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0405 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0405","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy0506 / ato_itr_inc_loss_0506","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy9900 / ato_itr_inc_loss_9900"]},{"n":"WHM_NET_INCM_AMT","d":"Income earned on a 417 or 462 working holiday visa less the deductions relating to it, the slice of a taxpayer's income taxed at the working holiday maker rate.","full":"Income earned on a 417 or 462 working holiday visa less the deductions relating to it, the slice of a taxpayer's income taxed at the working holiday maker rate. The ATO defines it as \"the income you earned or derived while you were on a 417 or 462 working holiday visa, less deductions relating to earning that income\", and notes that \"The first $37,000 of your working holiday maker net income is taxed at 15%. All other income is taxed according to your residency status.\" Employers flag the income with payment type H on the payment summary, which is how a taxpayer identifies it. The rate applied only from 1 January 2017, so the column's first year, 2015-16, precedes the measure and 2016-17 covers 1 January to 30 June 2017 alone.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2018, question A4 Working holiday maker net income","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2018/tax-return/adjustment-questions-a1-a4/a4-working-holiday-maker-net-income-2018","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Working holiday maker net income","k":"Dollar amount at item A4 Working holiday maker net income","def":"A whole-dollar net amount, self-assessed, floored at zero: gross working holiday maker income from all sources less the related deductions at items D1 to D10.","p":"2015-2016 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2018, question A4 Working holiday maker net income","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2018/tax-return/adjustment-questions-a1-a4/a4-working-holiday-maker-net-income-2018","lim":"It does not identify everyone who held a working holiday visa. Only income earned while on the visa counts, so a person who transitioned to another visa mid-year reports part of their earnings here and part in the ordinary items, and someone on the visa who did not work reports nothing. Because the column is net of deductions it also cannot be used as a wages measure.","where":["madip-ge-020129d-ato-atoitrincloss1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1516","madip-ge-020134d-ato-atoitrincloss1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1617","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1718","madip-ge-020139d-ato-atoitrincloss1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1819","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy1920 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1920","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy1920 / ato_itr_inc_loss_1920_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2021 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2021_12m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2021 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2021_16m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2021-22 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2122_12m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2223 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2223_12m","madipge-ato-d-inc-loss-fy2324 / ato_itr_inc_loss_2324_12m"]},{"n":"WRK_RLTD_CAR_EXPNSS_AMT","d":"The deduction claimed at label A of item D1 for using the taxpayer's own car for work.","full":"The deduction claimed at label A of item D1 for using the taxpayer's own car for work. The claim is a modelled figure rather than an expense record, because the ATO lets the taxpayer choose the calculation: \"If you have more than one car and you are claiming expenses under different methods, add the amounts you work out under each method and write the total at item D1 on your tax return.\" The claim type column on the same row says which method produced the largest amount and was therefore coded. The methods were cut from four to two in 2015-16, when only the cents per kilometre and logbook methods survived, which puts a structural break in the middle of the series.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2011/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d1-work-related-car-expenses-2011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Work related car expenses","k":"Dollar amount at label A, item D1 Work related car expenses","def":"A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction for the income year, totalled across cars and across calculation methods where more than one was used.","p":"1999-2000 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2011/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d1-work-related-car-expenses-2011","lim":"It is not the cost of running a car for work. Under the cents per kilometre and 12 per cent of original value methods the claim is a formula output that needs no receipts, so identical work travel can produce very different claims, and the 2015-16 change in available methods shifts the distribution independently of behaviour. It is also a claim, not an allowed amount, and includes claims later denied on review.","where":["madip-ge-020103d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1011","madip-ge-020108d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1112","madip-ge-020113d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1213","madip-ge-020118d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1314","madip-ge-020123d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1415","madip-ge-020128d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1516","madip-ge-020133d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1617","madip-ge-020138d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1718","madip-ge-020138d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1819","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0001 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0001","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0102 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0102","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0203 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0203","and 15 more"]},{"n":"WRK_RLTD_CAR_EXPNSS_CLM_TYP_CD","d":"The method the taxpayer used to work out the item D1 car deduction, printed in the CLAIM TYPE box beside label A.","full":"The method the taxpayer used to work out the item D1 car deduction, printed in the CLAIM TYPE box beside label A. Four codes were available on returns of this period: S for cents per kilometre, T for 12 per cent of original value, O for one-third of actual expenses and B for the logbook method. Where more than one car and method are involved the ATO says to \"Print the code letter for the method that gave you the largest amount in the CLAIM TYPE box\", so the code describes the dominant method, not every method used. From 2015-16 only the cents per kilometre and logbook methods remain, so T and O disappear from later years.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses, methods 1 to 4","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2011/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d1-work-related-car-expenses-2011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Work related car expenses - claim type","k":"Claim type code at item D1 (S, T, O or B)","def":"A single character in the claim type box at item D1, present only where a car expense deduction was claimed.","p":"1999-2000, 2000-2001, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004, 2004-2005, 2005-2006, 2006-2007, 2009-2010, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2011, question D1 Work-related car expenses, methods 1 to 4","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2011/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d1-work-related-car-expenses-2011","lim":"It does not partition the dollar amount beside it. Only four kinds of clothing qualify, named by the claim type column on the same row, and conventional clothing is excluded no matter how strictly an employer requires it. Substantiation is light at the bottom of the range: the ATO allows a taxpayer who launders at home to \"use a reasonable basis to calculate the amount, such as $1 per load for work-related clothing, or 50 cents per load if other laundry items were included\", and written evidence for laundry is needed only where the laundry claim is above $150 and the total work expense claim is above $300. Protective footwear and clothing come here, while other protective items such as hard hats and sunscreen are claimed at item D5.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3 Work-related clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning expenses","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d3-work-related-clothing-laundry-and-dry-cleaning-expenses-2012","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Work related clothing expenses","k":"Dollar amount at label C, item D3 Work related clothing expenses","def":"A whole-dollar self-assessed deduction combining the cost of eligible work clothing with laundry and dry-cleaning costs for the year.","p":"1999-2000 to 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3 Work-related clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning expenses","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d3-work-related-clothing-laundry-and-dry-cleaning-expenses-2012","lim":"It is not a record of spending. The laundry component is routinely estimated at a per-load rate, with no receipts required while the laundry claim stays under $150, so a large part of the mass of small claims is formula-driven, and the column cannot separate the clothing purchase from the washing. It also does not identify uniformed occupations, because occupation-specific and protective clothing sit in the same total as uniforms.","where":["madip-ge-020103d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1011","madip-ge-020108d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1112","madip-ge-020113d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1213","madip-ge-020118d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1314","madip-ge-020123d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1415","madip-ge-020128d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1516","madip-ge-020133d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1617","madip-ge-020138d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1718","madip-ge-020138d-ato-atoitrdedexpoff1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_1819","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0001 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0001","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0102 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0102","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0203 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0203","and 15 more"]},{"n":"WRK_RLTD_CLTHG_EXPNSS_TYP_CD","d":"The main kind of clothing behind the item D3 claim, printed as a single letter in the CLAIM TYPE box.","full":"The main kind of clothing behind the item D3 claim, printed as a single letter in the CLAIM TYPE box. The ATO's four codes are C for a compulsory work uniform, N for a non-compulsory work uniform, S for occupation-specific clothing and P for protective clothing. The taxpayer is asked to \"Select the code letter that describes the main type of clothing you are claiming for\", so the code is a dominant category rather than an exhaustive one. The distinction has consequences: a non-compulsory uniform is only deductible where the design is registered, while occupation-specific and protective clothing are deductible on their own terms.","dsrc":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3, step 3","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d3-work-related-clothing-laundry-and-dry-cleaning-expenses-2012","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Work related clothing expenses - claim type","k":"Claim type code at item D3 (C, N, S or P)","def":"A single character in the claim type box at item D3, present only where a clothing deduction was claimed.","p":"1999-2000, 2000-2001, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004, 2004-2005, 2005-2006, 2006-2007, 2009-2010, 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2012-2013, 2013-2014, 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question D3, step 3","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/paper-tax-return-instructions/2012/tax-return/deduction-questions-d1-d10/d3-work-related-clothing-laundry-and-dry-cleaning-expenses-2012","lim":"It cannot be used to split the deduction. A nurse claiming both a uniform and protective footwear reports one code and one amount, so the code understates the mix of clothing behind the claim. Nor is it an occupational classifier: the same code covers very different jobs, and the occupation code elsewhere on the return is the field for that question.","where":["madip-ge-020102d-ato-atoitrcontext1011-fy2010-11 / ato_itr_context_1011","madip-ge-020107d-ato-atoitrcontext1112-fy2011-12 / ato_itr_context_1112","madip-ge-020112d-ato-atoitrcontext1213-fy2012-13 / ato_itr_context_1213","madip-ge-020117d-ato-atoitrcontext1314-fy2013-14 / ato_itr_context_1314","madip-ge-020122d-ato-atoitrcontext1415-fy2014-15 / ato_itr_context_1415","madip-ge-020127d-ato-atoitrcontext1516-fy2015-16 / ato_itr_context_1516","madip-ge-020132d-ato-atoitrcontext1617-fy2016-17 / ato_itr_context_1617","madip-ge-020137d-ato-atoitrcontext1718-fy2017-18 / ato_itr_context_1718","madip-ge-020137d-ato-atoitrcontext1819-fy2018-19 / ato_itr_context_1819","madipge-ato-d-context-fy0001 / ato_itr_context_0001","madipge-ato-d-context-fy0102 / ato_itr_context_0102","madipge-ato-d-context-fy0203 / ato_itr_context_0203","and 13 more"]},{"n":"WRK_RLTD_DEDN_AMT","d":"A total of the work-related deduction items on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06.","full":"A total of the work-related deduction items on individual returns from 1999-2000 to 2005-06. The returns of this period carry the five work expense items separately, at labels A for car expenses, B for travel, C for clothing and laundry, D for self-education and E for other work expenses, with no printed total, so this column is an aggregate the ATO derived rather than a form label. A separate declared total sits beside it in the same table, which suggests the pair distinguishes an assessed total from the taxpayer's own. The five component columns for these years remain available, so the total can be checked against them.","dsrc":"ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), deduction items D1 to D5","durl":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=0976-6.2000","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Work Related Deduction Amount","k":"Dollar amount of total work-related deductions, pre-2006 returns","def":"A whole-dollar amount covering the work-related deduction items D1 to D5 of the individual return for the income year.","p":"1999-2000 to 2005-2006","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, TaxPack 2000 (NAT 0976), deduction items D1 to D5","url":"https://iorder.com.au/publication/Download.aspx?ProdID=0976-6.2000","lim":"Its relationship to the declared total on the same row is unstated, so it should not be assumed to equal the sum of the five component columns without testing. The $300 substantiation threshold of the period is also invisible here: a taxpayer claiming just under $300 without written evidence and one with full records produce indistinguishable figures.","where":["madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0001 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0001","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0102 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0102","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0203 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0203","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0304 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0304","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0405 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0405","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy0506 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_0506","madipge-ato-d-ded-exp-off-fy9900 / ato_itr_ded_exp_off_9900"]},{"n":"WRK_RLTD_OTHR_EXPNSS_AMT","d":"The deduction claimed at item D5 for work expenses with no item of their own.","full":"The deduction claimed at item D5 for work expenses with no item of their own. The ATO's list runs to union fees and professional association subscriptions, overtime meal expenses paid under a genuine allowance, seminars, courses and conferences, reference books and trade journals, tools, equipment and professional libraries, and \"items that protect you from the risk of injury or illness posed by your work or your work environment, such as hard hats, safety glasses and sunscreens (but not protective clothing and footwear, which you claim at item D3 )\". Home office and computer running costs are also claimed here, which is why the item grew sharply in the working-from-home years.
